svg.title: Where policy templates and custom code act on a connector call
svg.desc: A request from a flow action passes through the connector runtime of FieldLink Jobs version 1.1 before it reaches FieldLink, and the response passes back. Left: three actions, Create a job, Get a job and the internal List subcontractors. Middle top: request policies. setheader adds X-Client cedar-power-platform to every request. routerequesttoendpoint applies only to CreateJob and changes the path from /v1/jobs to /v2/jobs, keeping body and method. Middle bottom: custom code in script.csx, which runs only for the operations listed in scriptOperations, GetJob and ListSubcontractors. The script changes /v1/ to /v2/ itself, sends the request with Context.SendAsync, and transforms the version 2 answer: upper-case states to version 1 words, unknown words to unknown, events sorted into a timeline, and the subcontractors object into a sorted list for the dynamic values. Errors pass through unchanged. Right: FieldLink API version 2. Bottom note: code takes precedence over the codeless definition for its operations; Learn does not document the order of policies and code in one call, so Cedar never puts a routing policy on an operation the script handles; preview templates are not used in Cedar-Prod.
svg.text: FieldLink Jobs v1.1: one connector, two ways to change a call at run time
Codeless, declarative, scoped by operation name
new words → unknown, events → sorted timeline,
Code takes precedence over the codeless definition for the operations it handles. One script per connector, .NET Standard 2.0,
only the documented namespaces, at most 2 minutes and 1 MB; Context.SendAsync instead of your own HttpClient.
Learn does not document the order of policies and code within one call: Cedar never puts a routing policy on a scripted operation.
Templates marked (preview) on Learn (convert object to array, set property, …) stay out of connectors released to Cedar-Prod.
